meta.title: BitSpring — free bit-perfect music player for macOS and Windows
meta.description: A free music player that sends your DAC exactly what is in the file. FLAC, ALAC, WAV, DSD up to DSD1024, up to 768 kHz. EQ, crossfeed and upsampling when you want them.
meta.og_description: A free bit-perfect music player for macOS and Windows.
hero.title: Bit for bit
hero.lede: A free music player for macOS and Windows. Your DAC gets exactly what is in the file: no resampling, no system mixer, no surprises.
cta.appstore: Download on the Mac App Store
cta.appstore_soon: Coming to the Mac App Store
path.title: Not a single bit changes between the file and the DAC
path.file_detail: FLAC, 24-bit, 96 kHz. Samples are read exactly as stored.
path.player_detail: Doesn't resample, doesn't touch the volume, doesn't mix in system sounds.
path.dac_detail: The player takes exclusive control of it and switches it to 96 kHz, the file's own rate.
path.foot: On macOS: CoreAudio exclusive (hog) mode with integer output. On Windows: WASAPI Exclusive.
formats.title: From CD to 768 kHz
formats.lede: The player switches your DAC to each track's sample rate. If the DAC can't do that rate, the audio is carefully resampled, and the player tells you so.
formats.dsd: DSD plays natively over DoP if your DAC supports it, or as 176.4 kHz PCM if it doesn't.
formats.files: FLAC, ALAC, WAV, AIFF, CAF, MKA, DSF, DFF, MP3, AAC, Ogg Vorbis
enhance.title: Want a different sound? Go ahead
enhance.lede: Enhancers are off by default. Turn any of them on and the player's indicator switches from "Bit-perfect" to "Processing" and lists exactly what is being done to the sound.
enhance.upsampling_detail: To 192, 384 or 768 kHz, for DACs that sound better at high rates.
enhance.eq_detail: Load an AutoEQ profile for your headphones. Filters are computed with 64-bit precision.
enhance.crossfeed_detail: Light, medium or strong. Removes the feeling that the music is playing inside your head.
enhance.lossy_detail: Headroom against clipping turns on by itself, and the highs above the codec's cutoff can be gently restored.
app.title: Everything that happens to the sound, in plain sight
app.lede: File format, DAC sample rate and every processing step, right on the main screen.
app.alt: The player window: queue, now playing, and the Bit-perfect indicator with the signal path
download.title: Free
download.lede: No subscription, no ads, no account. Just a player.
dl.meta_title: Download BitSpring for macOS, Windows, iPhone and Android
dl.meta_description: Get the free bit-perfect music player for your device.
dl.title: Download BitSpring
dl.appstore_note: Installs and updates through the App Store.
dl.mac_file_note: Open it and drag BitSpring into Applications.
dl.mac_file_hint: The first time, macOS stops it: open System Settings → Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway.
dl.windows_file_hint: If SmartScreen stops it, click More info, then Run anyway.
dl.android_hint: Android 9 or later, 64-bit. Allow your browser to install apps when asked.
privacy.meta_description: BitSpring collects nothing: no account, no analytics, no ads, no tracking.
privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.lead: BitSpring collects nothing about you. There is no account, no analytics, no advertising and no tracking.
privacy.device: Your music, playlists, equalizer presets and settings stay on your device. The app uploads none of them.
privacy.network: The app goes online only for what you ask of it. The version from this website asks GitHub whether there is an update and downloads it; GitHub sees what any download shows, your IP address and the app version. If you sign in to Qobuz or TIDAL, the app talks to that service alone, and your sign-in stays on your device. The App Store versions don't go online at all.
privacy.site: This website sets no cookies and runs no analytics. Your browser remembers the language you picked, and that never leaves it. Like any web host, Vercel keeps standard server logs.
privacy.open: BitSpring is open source, so anyone can check all of this in its code.
